channel.title: Awaitful for Mac
channel.description: Updates for the Awaitful macOS app.

item.title: Version 0.1.2
item.description:
• Awaitful now earns while OpenAI Codex is thinking: in the ChatGPT app (Codex and Work modes), in the terminal, and in VS Code. Codex asks you once to approve the hooks Awaitful adds, and Settings shows how far that has got and opens Codex for you when it is needed.
  • Claude Code earns in the Claude app's Code mode too. The Agents section now says where each agent works.
  • Each agent is followed on its own. When two work at once the ad stays up while either is thinking, and one agent never keeps it up for the other.
  • If one of Awaitful's Codex hooks is switched off, Awaitful pauses ads for Codex and says how to switch it back on. A conversation that was open at the time cannot say when it stops, so ads for Codex wait until you quit and reopen the app it is in.
  • Ads come down more reliably when your agent stops.
  • The ad has a new look: a capsule that fits its whole line, with the Awaitful logo, in light and dark mode. Pick its border color in Ad Format: a new one each time your agent starts thinking, one you choose, or Monochrome to match the other icons in your menu bar.
  • Ad Format shows a picture of each format. Click one to choose it, and click where the desktop panel should sit on a picture of your screen.
  • Pause Awaitful and Resume Awaitful in the menu say what they do, and the menu and buttons have symbols. Check for updates from Settings, under General.
  • `--uninstall` now asks before it changes anything, removes everything Awaitful put on your Mac, and tells you what is left to do. Add `--yes` to skip the question, or `--forget-approvals` to also clear Codex's record of approving Awaitful, so installing again starts fresh.

item.title: Version 0.1.1
item.description:
• Settings has a sidebar. General, Agents and Ad Format sit down the left the way sections do in Finder and System Settings, with room for the settings still to come.
  • Settings now looks like the macOS you are running. The sidebar, switches and grouped boxes are drawn by your Mac, so they match it on this release of macOS and the next.
  • New Agents section. See which coding agents Awaitful found on this Mac and connect or disconnect each one. If an agent is not installed, it says so rather than asking you to connect it.
  • Linking this Mac now sits at the top of General. Once it is linked, Awaitful connects to the coding agents it finds and tells you it has. Connecting adds one line to your agent's own settings file and never changes the agent itself. If you disconnect an agent, it stays disconnected until you connect it again.
  • Opening Awaitful again from Finder or Spotlight now shows Settings. It used to appear to do nothing, because a menu bar app has no window to bring forward.
  • Awaitful can take itself back out cleanly. Before deleting the app, run `/Applications/Awaitful.app/Contents/MacOS/Awaitful --uninstall` in Terminal. It removes the lines Awaitful added to your agent's settings and stops it opening at login, and leaves everything else in those files alone.

item.title: Version 0.1.0
item.description:
First release for macOS.

  • Awaitful now works without a code editor. It shows one sponsored line while your coding agent is thinking, and you earn while that line is genuinely on screen.
  • Choose where it appears: a line in your menu bar, or a small panel near the top of your screen.
  • Link this Mac to your account once, and it earns alongside anything else you already have running.
  • Awaitful can open when you log in, so it is ready before your first agent run.
  • Awaitful never reads your code, your prompts, or anything your agent says. It detects only that an agent is working, and for how long.
